title: Arrears Rate Note — What a Plan Year Difference Bears Where Instalments Have Stopped
content:
Where instalments on an account under Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts stopped being billed some months before the plan year was settled, the difference arrived at bears a monthly rate. How long the instalments have been stopped, taken with the size of the year's cost against the balance the programme will carry, decides the rate.

**Where an instalment was last billed on the account at least 3 months ago and the year's cost stands above the programme's credit ceiling**, the rate the difference bears is the programme's monthly service charge.

**Where an instalment was last billed on the account at least 3 months ago and the year's cost stands at or under the programme's credit ceiling**, the rate the difference bears is the programme's monthly service charge less 0.5 of a percentage point.

**Where an instalment was billed on the account more recently than 3 months ago**, the rate the difference bears is nothing.

## Reading the two tests

| Whole months since an instalment was last billed | The year's cost against the programme's credit ceiling | The rate the difference bears |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 or more | Above the ceiling | The programme's monthly service charge |
| 3 or more | At or under the ceiling | The programme's monthly service charge, less 0.5 |
| Fewer than 3 | Either way | Nothing |

The months are whole months counted from the day the most recent instalment was billed to the handling date, and the ceiling is the balance the catalogue says the programme will carry.

*Hypothetical.* An account on a programme whose monthly service charge is 1.5 percent and whose credit ceiling is 6000.00 USD was last billed an instalment 4 months ago, and its year's cost comes to 6400.00 USD. The cost stands above the ceiling, so the difference bears 1.5 percent a month. Had the year's cost come to 6000.00 USD exactly, it would stand at the ceiling and the rate would be 1.0 percent a month. Had an instalment been billed 2 months ago, the rate would be nothing on either figure.
